before: Whatever event you pass to a handler must match `RequestEvent`. Register your event's type in the `ServerTypes` registry in `@nuxt/schema`, which is what `NuxtRequestEvent` and `useRequestEvent()` resolve to. If your own event object isn't web-shaped, pass handlers a web-shaped view of it (`toNuxtRequestEvent()` returns one) and put your own event on the `~app` property, so `useRequestEvent()` and the render hooks give app code your event instead.
after: Whatever event you pass to a handler must match `RequestEvent`. Register your event's type in the `ServerTypes` registry in `@nuxt/schema`, which is what `NuxtRequestEvent` and `useRequestEvent()` resolve to. If your own event object isn't web-shaped, pass handlers a web-shaped view of it. To give app code your own event instead, set it as `~app` on the event you pass the [renderer](#standing-up-the-ssr-renderer).

before: Nuxt provides a private `runtimeConfig.appSecret` as the application's root secret. Modules and server features can use it to derive their own secrets. The value defaults to an empty string, is only available on the server, and you can set it with `NUXT_APP_SECRET` without declaring the key in `nuxt.config`.
after: Nuxt provides a private `runtimeConfig.appSecret` as the application's root secret. Modules and server features derive their own secrets from it with [`deriveSecret`](/docs/guide/going-further/server-imports#deriving-secrets), and the [session helpers](/docs/guide/going-further/server-imports#sessions) seal with one by default. The value defaults to an empty string, is only available on the server, and you can set it with `NUXT_APP_SECRET` without declaring the key in `nuxt.config`.

before: In API routes, using `createError` by passing an object with a short `statusText` is recommended because it can be accessed on the client side. Otherwise, a `message` passed to `createError` on an API route will not propagate to the client. Alternatively, you can use the `data` property to pass data back to the client. In any case, always consider avoiding to put dynamic user input to the message to avoid potential security issues.
after: In API routes, using `createError` by passing an object with a short `statusText` is recommended because it can be accessed on the client side. Otherwise, a `message` passed to `createError` on an API route will not propagate to the client. Alternatively, you can use the `data` property to pass data back to the client. When handling the error with `useFetch`, the custom data is available at `error.value.data.data`. In any case, always consider avoiding to put dynamic user input to the message to avoid potential security issues.

before: Nitro is an open source TypeScript framework to build ultra-fast web servers. Nuxt uses Nitro as its server engine. before: Static site generation (SSG) with `ssr: true` pre-renders routes of your application at build time. (This is the default behavior when running `nuxt generate`.)
